name: Dubinky Well Road — marked primitive camping sites
rules: Use only a brown-post/tent-symbol designated primitive site; do not camp at the coordinate simply because it marks road access. Official BLM camping map identifies designated primitive sites as free; separate paid Lone Mesa Group Sites are not this recommendation. No ordinary overnight permit stated in reviewed Moab sources. 14 days at one location, then relocate at least 30 miles. Carry out solid human waste; portable toilet required where no constructed toilet provided. Road access reference is about 21.6 miles from Moab; USU describes 2WD on main routes, high-clearance / 4WD on secondary routes. No general passenger-car guarantee for every marked site. No woodcutting or gathering; obey current fire restrictions.

name: Cinder Hills Off Highway Vehicle Area
rules: Use the designated motorized recreation/camping area beyond any posted no-camping entrance area; no individual pad invented. No fee stated on current official page; do not label a paid campground. No ordinary overnight camping permit is stated on the current official page. 14 days in any consecutive 30 days under order 03-04-00-26-08. 13 miles northeast of downtown Flagstaff, reached by FR 776 from US 89. The November 23 road status lists FR 776 open. Loose cinders and rough roads mean passenger-car access is not guaranteed everywhere. No potable water. No glass containers. Nearby Sunset Crater National Monument and Strawberry Crater Wilderness closed to OHV travel.

name: West Sedona — eight designated dispersed camping areas
rules: Camp only inside one of the eight designated areas; arbitrary FR 525 roadside pullouts prohibited within the wider order area. Free. No reservation required; first come, first served. 14 days; the forestwide limit of 14 days in any 30 days also applies. FR 525 between SR 89A and FR 152C was listed open November 23. This does not guarantee every inner spur is suitable for a passenger car. No wood or charcoal fires at any time; LPG stoves and grills with an on/off control are permitted. No potable water.

name: Jean/Roach Dry Lakes — BLM dispersed recreation area
rules: Dispersed camping is an official listed use of this recreation area. No camping fee stated on official page; not independently verified as a zero-dollar fee. No ordinary overnight permit is stated on the official page. 14 days in any 28 days; then people and property must relocate outside a 25-mile radius, or to land not managed by BLM, for 14 days. Official directions place this area about 26 miles south of Las Vegas: I-15 Sloan exit 25 to Las Vegas Boulevard, then Knight Ranch Road. Outside the dry lakebed use existing roads and trails only. After precipitation the lakebed may retain deep water for a long time. BLM advises against driving on it after rain. Ground conditions are separate from camping permission.

Gross Reservoir expansion can cause other intermittent closures.

name: Slate River · Musicians Camp MC1–17 designated roadside sites
rules: Only Forest Service numbered posts with universal camping symbols. Unnumbered nearby pullouts are forbidden within the order boundary. Maximum 14 days; leaving property unattended over 24 hours prohibited. First come, first served. No live availability feed. Current USFS page lists restroom facilities at Musicians Camp. Only provided metal rings, subject to current fire restrictions.
